question: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation contains a phased implementation timetable, with strict requirements for recyclability, recycled content, minimisation, empty space, reuse and specific packaging bans. There is deep anxiety among smaller businesses and distributors, particularly in relation to whether or not they will be required to register an authorised representative in each of the 27 Member States.
The Commission’s failure to properly communicate the new rules to businesses has led to some reporting a cessation in some of their services due to the lack of clarity. 1.
Can the Commission outline what businesses, if any, are exempt from this new regulation?
Is it necessary for all businesses to register an authorised representative in each EU Member State?
Will the Commission consider a derogation for smaller businesses?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 (PPWR) lays down several exemptions for smaller businesses as regards certain obligations2. Micro-enterprises are exempt from the obligations imposed on ‘manufacturers’ and ‘producers’ under certain circumstances.

They benefit from exemptions from the re-use targets (Article 29) and re-use obligations in the packaging used in the take-away sector (Article 33). As regards extended producer responsibility, the PPWR includes flexibilities and exemptions designed to make life easier for small producers producing less than 10 tonnes of packaging per year.

It also requires Member States and producer responsibility organisations (PRO) not to place disproportionate burden on small producers. The Commission is actively calling on Member States to make use of such flexibilities, for example by exempting small businesses from registration fees, introducing flat fees, and limiting administrative and reporting procedures3.

The PPWR requires businesses to appoint authorised representatives in Member States in which they sell packaged products directly to consumers. In December 2025, the Commission proposed to suspend this obligation to minimise administrative burdens and costs for businesses. The Environmental Omnibus4 is being examined by the European Parliament and the Council.

The Commission urges the co-legislators to come to a swift agreement to ensure that producers who put small quantities of products on the Single Market benefit from its full potential ahead of the high-demand retail period. Further reforms of the extended producer responsibility are also being considered in the context of the upcoming Circular Economy Act.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/482959c3-cc2d-11f1-8b4c-01aa75ed71a1/language-en. 3 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/topics/waste-and-recycling/packaging-waste/extended-producerresponsibility-packaging-small-businesses_en. 4 https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/files/attachment/882049/Factsheet-EnvironmentalOmnibus.pdf.
